overview: Two connected organelles in the cell's manufacturing and shipping line — one processes proteins, the other packages and ships them onward.
genZNote: ER: the factory floor. Golgi: the packaging and shipping department.

aspects.label: Structure
aspects.valueA: A stack of flattened, curved membranous sacs (cisternae), not directly continuous with the nuclear envelope.
aspects.valueB: A network of interconnected membranous tubules and sacs, continuous with the nuclear envelope.

aspects.label: Main Function
aspects.valueA: Modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids received from the ER, then ships them to their destinations.
aspects.valueB: Synthesises proteins (rough ER) and lipids (smooth ER), and folds/modifies new proteins.

aspects.label: Types / Subdivisions
aspects.valueA: A single continuous structure with cis, medial, and trans faces.
aspects.valueB: Divided into rough ER (ribosome-studded) and smooth ER (no ribosomes).

aspects.label: Position in the Pathway
aspects.valueA: Receives material from the ER via transport vesicles; comes after ER in the secretory pathway.
aspects.valueB: The first stop for newly made proteins entering the secretory pathway.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Proteins travel ER → Golgi (cis to trans face) → secretory vesicle — a frequently drawn NEET diagram.
overlay.memoryTrick: ER makes it. Golgi finishes, wraps, and mails it.
overlay.commonMisconception: The Golgi apparatus does not synthesise proteins itself — it only modifies and packages what the ER already made.
